messages:
nora: Quick flag from today— while onboarding magnet-32k int4 we observed a cache "split+resume" mismatch. Prefill ~11.7k, second append ~9k, resume generation; occasionally a short run (5-7 tokens) repeats and subsequent KV fingerprint changes. Intermittent (~1/300).

sam: Where are you running this? Dedicated QA or local env? Any repro harness?

nora: Dedicated QA (ded-qa-7). I have a tiny script that issues two requests: prefill then append then resume streaming. Pushing to /tmp/magnet_split_repro.sh.

vik: Sounds like a phasing continuity issue (RoPE-related) when stitching prefill KV with live in-flight cache. Do you see any posscale or posshift adjustments logged?

nora: No explicit posscale adjustments. Here's the short log from a failing trace: 

```
[cache] prefill id=0x7f2a fp=0x9b2c len=11712 shard_slot=10
[cache] append id=0x7f2b fp=0x9b2d len+=9216 shard_slot=10
gen: step=11718 tok=1012 dup_window=11714-11719 detected
[cache] postappend_fp=0x9b2d != expected_fp=0x9b2c
```

vik: fp changed even though shard_slot is same. Could be a write-order race where append metadata races with the in-flight generation snapshot.

tasha: Have you tried the control where kv_policy=reset between requests? That would isolate whether folding is causing state mismatch.

nora: Yes, reset fixes it every time but the latency cost is too high for our target (adds ~20ms P50). We want kv_policy=fold to be safe.

sam: Another thought: are we honoring the same epoch/seq-id across split and append? If append carries a new epoch without merging epoch deltas, the fingerprint calc will diverge. Can you dump the epoch headers?

nora: Epoch headers from the failing run: prefill_epoch=42, append_epoch=42, seq_base=0x1a3. No mismatch shown.

ci-bot: Created issue #4481: "magnet-32k: intermittent split-resume duplication under kv_fold" (reporter: nora) :bug: 

vik: Plan: 1) add a tight unit test that mocks the two-request flow with deterministic RNG and quantized kernels (qemu-enabled) to try 50k iterations locally; 2) add a temporary lock around append->merge to check if race goes away; 3) capture full KV slot dumps when failure occurs for forensic.

nora: I'll add the unit test and push to the onboarding branch. Also uploading token dumps to /artifacts/magnet32k/snap-1798642001.tar.gz.

sam: If lock makes it disappear, we need a lighter-weight fix than global mutex. Maybe compare-and-swap on fingerprint update or a small epoch handshake between append and active generator.

tasha: Also try toggling the RoPE clamp behavior in the stitcher: small experiments where we force continuous pos offset vs. re-evaluated pos embeddings on append. That will tell if the issue is from misapplied rotational phase.

nora: Good call. I'll run both experiments in perf-lab tomorrow morning. If we can reliably reproduce under qemu with int4 kernels we avoid burning Dedicated capacity.

vik: One more note: therewas an async footgun in the append path where metadata merges without a memory barrier on architectures with weak ordering. On x86 it might be rare, but on ARM64 it could be more frequent. Make sure the unit test runs on both archs.

ci-bot: CI patchset 7921 created for branch "onboard/magnet32k/split-fix" and assigned to @vik.

sam: Thanks. Keep the thread updated. If repro rate goes up we can schedule a quick postmortem and consider a small hotfix to the runtime before broad rollout.

nora: Will update after the 50k deterministic run. TLDR: intermittent duplication at prefill-append join, fingerprint drift, kv_policy=reset workaround; investigating race vs. RoPE continuity. :mag:
